newsitem.title: USA: Conrail chair may get $22 mln parachute-NYT.
newsitem.headline: Conrail chair may get $22 mln parachute-NYT.

text.p: Conrail Inc chairman David LeVan could get a $22 million golden parachute if Federal regulators approved a proposed deal to split the railroad company between CSX Corp and Norfolk Southern Corp, the New York Times reported on Friday.
CSX and Norfolk Southern, who fought a prolonged takeover battle for Conrail, began to prepare negotiations on Monday for the final division of the railroad company.

Under a recently-revised merger deal, CSX was to pay Conrail shareholders $115 per share in cash, or about $10.3 billion, and would be allowed to negotiate a division of Conrail with rival bidder Norfolk Southern.
LeVan would receive more than 40 times the $539,278 in salary and bonuses he received at Conrail in 1995, the paper said, citing a person close to the negotiations.
Other top managers who were dismissed would also receive large benefits, the paper said, quoting the source.
All 79 senior managers at Conrail were expected to be dismissed, according to forecasts provided by the person familiar with the talks, the newspaper said.
Depending on the length of their employment, they were expected to get about $1.5 million each in severances, bonuses and disbursements from the employee stock plan, the Times said.
The 1,187 nonunion secretaries, engineers and midlevel managers whose jobs were expected to be eliminated were to receive an average of $420,000, it said.
Conrail, CSX and Norfolk Southern were not immediately available for comment.
